theme: The gap between an event people attend and one they talk about for years

linkedin.text:
The data on corporate events is uncomfortable.

Most employees can't recall the key message of the last all-hands they attended. Most incentive trip participants have forgotten the destination within a year. Most conference themes disappear the moment the slides do.

The companies whose events beat those averages have one thing in common: they briefed their production partner on outcomes, not just logistics.

Uproduction Events has worked that way for 16 years — 1,500+ events, 130+ destinations, 25,000+ participants. The brief that matters is the one that starts with 'what do we need this team to feel, decide, or do differently after this?'

I'm curious: what's the last corporate event you attended that actually changed something? Drop it in the comments — no judgment on the ones that didn't. 👇

instagram.text:
Most corporate events are forgotten within a week. 📉

130+ destinations. 1,500+ events. 25,000+ people who went home with something to say.

facebook.text:
There's a difference between an event people show up to — and one they still talk about two years later.

The gap isn't budget. It's not the venue. It's not even the speaker lineup.

It's whether someone thought hard about what should happen between the agenda items.

We've helped HR and marketing leaders close that gap at 1,500+ events across 130+ destinations. The ones who notice it most are the attendees — and the executives watching retention data three months later.

What does a genuinely memorable corporate event look like to you? Tell us in the comments. 👇
